statement: The Itinerary prints that on 5 July, leaving Gettysburg, the Second Corps marched to Two Taverns and the Artillery Reserve to Littlestown; the Second Corps' own artillery brigade is not named separately.
reasoning: The Itinerary prints the march of the Second Corps to Two Taverns on 5 July and sends the Artillery Reserve separately to Littlestown; the artillery brigade of the Second Corps belonged to the corps (Hazard prints that it moved with the corps at daylight on 2 July) and the Itinerary names no separate march for it, so it marched with the corps; no report of the brigade prints the hour or the road.

statement: The Itinerary of the Army of the Potomac prints that on 5 July, leaving Gettysburg, the Second Corps marched to Two Taverns, the Fifth Corps to Marsh Run, the Sixth to Fairfield, the Eleventh to Rock Creek, the Twelfth to Littlestown and the Artillery Reserve to Littlestown.
reasoning: The Itinerary prints the march of the Second Corps from Gettysburg to Two Taverns on 5 July without an hour; Two Taverns stands on the Baltimore Pike by the road identification of McMichael's report (53d Pennsylvania), who marched on that road to Two Taverns on the same day.
